title: A refused suno/mv apply wrote the candidates that sorted before the refusal
evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/suno.ts:166-175 and lib/decision/v1/sources/mv.ts:313-322 (pre-fix): the held-verdict check sat inside the write loop; patchMv (lib/sound/mv/queue.ts:291-304) deletes DROPPED_FILES on a drop
body:
## Summary
The suno and mv appliers checked each candidate's held verdict inside the write loop, so a permanent refusal on a later candidate left the earlier ones written.

## Description
suno.ts/mv.ts apply walked the decisions sorted by key and refused on the first clip/job marked otherwise in v1 since - after patching every earlier one. For mv an earlier drop had already deleted its render files. A refusal is permanent (stuck), so v1 kept half an outcome nobody committed whole (hitl-approval resume-after-decision: re-validate the world before acting). Fixed: every candidate (gone, or marked otherwise) is checked before the first write, same sentences.

## Flow
- operator commits sc-a keep + sc-b drop
- Sound lab marks sc-b keep before the apply
- apply: sc-a patched, then refused on sc-b -> row stuck with sc-a written (mv: mj-a's 3 files deleted)

## Expected impact
An operator resolving a stuck suno/mv apply finds v1 exactly as the commit found it. Could break: nothing - the write loop is unchanged after the check.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused apply writes none of itself
Before: suno: sc-a = keep after a refusal on sc-b; mv: 3 render files of mj-a deleted after a refusal on mj-b
After: sc-a = null; 0 files deleted (seeded red on HEAD: 2 failed; green after)
Method: gate - two new assertions in decision-v1-suno/-mv
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A render sweep that outlived its claim left no trace
evidence: lib/decision/v1/applier.ts:112-113 (pre-fix) logged only !closed.ok; packages/kernel/src/ingest.ts:140-146 finishClaim returns ok(false) when the row names another owner
body:
## Summary
reconcileApplies dropped finishClaim's ok(false), the only signal that a sweep outlived its TTL and another reader took the claim.

## Description
When a sweep runs past APPLY_TTL_MS another reader may take decision-apply and sweep beside it; finishClaim then matches no row and returns ok(false). Only the err branch was logged. Now the false is logged with the claim and its TTL. Mirrors wave 1's 'A reaped applier's late report left no trace' for the sweep claim rather than the row lease.

## Flow
- reader A takes the claim and starts a slow sweep
- TTL passes; reader B takes the claim
- A's finishClaim returns ok(false) -> previously silent

## Expected impact
A lease/TTL too short for the drain becomes visible in the server log. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: observability - a lost sweep claim is reported
Before: 0 log lines when the claim was lost
After: 1 console.error naming the claim; a closed claim still 0 (seeded red: 1 failed)
Method: gate - decision-v1-seam sweep case + mutant decision-apply-sweep-lost-silent
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A keep's v1 reasons were disclosed as 'not forge/extract reasons'
evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/forge.ts:267 and lib/decision/v1/sources/extract.ts:248 (pre-fix); the correct spelling is lib/decision/v1/sources/strips.ts:176
body:
## Summary
On a keep every reason is lost to the note, but forge and extract named the loss as words outside their lists - false for list words like 'style'.

## Description
importVerdict gives reasons to a reject only, so on a keep `lost` holds all of them; the loss sentence still said 'are not forge reasons'. strips said it right. Both now say 'v1 reason(s)/tag(s) on a keep (...) ride in the note; only a reject carries reasons'; a reject's off-list words keep their sentence.

## Flow
- v1 keep with note 'reasons: style'
- packet() -> loss 'v1 reason(s) style are not forge reasons'

## Expected impact
The Board's disclosure of what the import lost is true. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a disclosure states the real reason
Before: 2 of 3 reason-importing adapters disclosed a keep's list word falsely
After: 0 of 3 (seeded red: 2 failed)
Method: gate - one packet() case per adapter
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A refused proof apply had already landed the verdicts before it
evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/proof.ts:183-207 (pre-fix): standing checked per proof inside the op loop; the pair of c0fc9019
body:
## Summary
The proof applier refused a proof judged otherwise since only after the earlier verdicts had landed as judge-proof ops.

## Description
Same shape as the suno/mv apply: a permanent refusal mid-loop left the style's log holding half the outcome (rev +3 where the atelier made one op). One rule `standing` now decides held/refused/may-run, read once over the style before any op and again per op inside the bounded conflict retry. The two mutants guarding the moved lines were re-pointed and re-killed.

## Flow
- commit p1 keep, p2 keep, p3 reject
- atelier approves p3
- apply: p1, p2 approved, then refused on p3

## Expected impact
A stuck proof apply leaves the style as the commit found it. Could break: a race between the pre-check and an op still refuses at the op, as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused apply writes none of itself
Before: p1, p2 approved; style rev +3
After: p1, p2 pending; rev +1 (seeded red: 1 failed)
Method: gate - decision-v1-proof refusal case
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The sweep TTL's comment claimed a full drain; the value is two leases
body:
## Summary
APPLY_TTL_MS was documented as 'a full drain at the lease each' (960 s) while set to LEASE_MS * 2 (240 s).

## Description
Corrected the doc to the value it has, why not a full drain (a crashed reader would block render sweeps 16 min), and what a slower sweep does.

## Flow
- read the constant's doc
- compute RENDER_MAX x LEASE_MS

## Expected impact
The next reader does not 'fix' the value to match a wrong comment. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - doc matches code
Before: stated TTL off by 720 s
After: 0
Method: probe - arithmetic over the two files
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Dojo and strips read hash media serially, two stats per file
instrument: a timed dojo/strips read() over a seeded 48-arm fixture of ~2 MB files with an empty digest cache (fresh process), plus a stat counter: ms and stats/file before vs after routing the resolved paths through mediaRefs (concurrency 8)
evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/dojo.ts:104-117 and lib/decision/v1/sources/strips.ts:85-97 await trainingFileStat/stripFileStat then mediaRef one file at a time; forge.ts:122 and extract.ts:138 use mediaRefs (lib/decision/v1/types.ts:211)
body:
## Summary
dojo.ts and strips.ts read each arm's file one at a time (resolver stat, then mediaRef's own stat and sha256), while forge/extract hash through mediaRefs eight at a time.

## Description
The first open of a dojo cycle or strip run hashes every arm/clip serially. Resolve paths with v1's resolver first (still per file), then hand the {key, abs} list to mediaRefs. Whether it is faster depends on cold-disk I/O vs single-thread hashing - hence B.

## Flow
- resolve each rel through v1's resolver
- mediaRefs(files) bounded at 8

## Expected impact
First open of a large cycle/strip run. Could break: an 'invalid' resolver answer must still be skipped, not fatal.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - first-open latency
Before: serial: 2 stats + 1 hash per file (walked)
After: predicted 1 resolver stat per file, hashing overlapped
Method: simulation - no timed fixture this round
Result: better
Gate: none

body:
## Summary
When v1's path resolver refuses a file, the adapter skips it silently and the packet's loss says the file is not on disk.

## Description

## Flow

- read(): filePathAbs throws -> skipped
- packet(): loss '<path> is not on disk'

## Expected impact
A corrupt record is reported as what it is. Could break: V1 type gains a field (tests that build literals).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a loss names its real cause
Before: 3 sites misreport a refusal as absence
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked the three read() paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The media digest cache clears whole at 4096 entries
body:
## Summary
digests.clear() at DIGEST_CACHE_MAX drops hot entries with cold ones.

## Description
A clear costs one rehash of the hot set per 4096 new files; an LRU over a cyclic scan larger than the cap misses as often. No figure favours a change.

## Flow
- walk a hot run plus a stream of new files under both policies

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance
Before: one hot-set rehash per 4096 new files
After: same order under LRU
Method: simulation - three access patterns walked
Result: not-better
Gate: none
